why: B moved more traffic in the migration itself — the host unlock (with loopback/private-network exclusion) means the configurations this repo actually ships route, where A leaves the default Anthropic-compat deployment on the provider pending an approval branch — and B's system-level work is sharper for this specific app: the stale MULTIMODAL_MODELS gate that silently strips the browser agent's screenshots on every current model is the one real correctness bug Router can't paper over, and B found, fixed and measured it. A's set is broader and better ranked, and its retry-predicate fix is a genuine win B not only misses but cites approvingly as a reason to skip fallbacks; it doesn't outweigh B shipping the cache key, spend label and server-side timeouts together while A left timeouts as a proposal.
A_best: The measured retry fix: retrying on bare Exception six times with 60s backoff inside a 20-step agent loop in front of a gateway with a spend cap is exactly the pathology to kill, and the before/after (6 requests/13s → 1 request/1.4s on a provider-rejected payload) proves it; the per-agent spend labels and the per-key spend-cap decision show the same autonomous-agent cost thinking.
B_best: Deriving the vision allowlist from Router's catalog — a real, app-specific defect (screenshots dropped on Claude 4.x/5, GPT-5.x) verified both side-by-side and live — paired with a migration that actually routes the shipped host configs and a model map whose target was chosen for same price and same sampling (sonnet-4-6) rather than the cheaper id that rejects temperature.
A_worst: Half the operational levers are proposals, not branches (provider_timeout, fallbacks, Bedrock, chart tool), and the one built unlock maps the shipped 3.7 Sonnet config to claude-sonnet-5, which silently drops the app's unconditional temperature=0.0 — a behaviour change B explicitly reasoned its way out of.
B_worst: It treats app/llm.py's retry-everything-six-times loop as a feature (using it to argue against fallbacks) instead of recognising it as a retry-storm bug in front of a metered gateway, and it offers no account-side guardrail (spend cap) for an agent that can loop 30 steps unattended.
